open_points.subject: project context confidentiality
open_points.text: “read a project context” returns “customer”, while “every read of contact data” requires a credential and personal data is “readable by staff only”
open_points.question: Does the unauthenticated context contain only `customer_ref` and erasure state, or any Customer name, phone, e-mail or language?
options: Only the customer reference and non-contact state
An embedded Customer object with contact fields omitted
Contact data, making context credential-protected
open_points.default_guess: Return only the customer reference and non-contact state.

open_points.subject: meaning of trusted host processes
open_points.text: “Every process and container on Registry's host is the owner's and trusted”
open_points.question: What is a host process trusted to do, given that writes and contact-data reads still require scoped credentials?
options: Trusted only not to expose the host-only network or misuse open data
Trusted with all Registry data and operations, with credentials as defense in depth
Mutually untrusted and limited strictly by credentials
open_points.default_guess: Trusted only not to expose the host-only network or misuse open data; credential rules remain authorization boundaries.

open_points.subject: operator direct-store authority
open_points.text: The operator “holds the staff credential for every action it takes” but an agent “could read the store itself” using “the owner's own access to Registry's host”
open_points.question: Is direct store access by the operator an authorized operating path, merely an acknowledged capability that must not be used, or limited to emergency inspection; and may it ever write the store?
options: API access only; direct access is an acknowledged threat capability
Direct read-only access is authorized
Direct read and write access is authorized
open_points.default_guess: Require normal operator work to use the API and treat direct access as an acknowledged capability, never an authorized write path.

open_points.subject: operator access to Registry secrets
open_points.text: An agent works with “the owner's own access to Registry's host”, while instance configuration is “readable only by the owner and the Registry process” and the operator “holds no service token”
open_points.question: Can an agent acting through the owner's host access read Registry's secret-bearing configuration, or is that access technically separated from the owner's configuration access?
options: The agent cannot read secret-bearing configuration
The agent can technically read it but is forbidden to do so
The agent is allowed to read it and therefore can obtain service tokens
open_points.default_guess: Separate the agent's access so it cannot read secret-bearing configuration.

open_points.subject: model provider boundary
open_points.text: “whatever it records or reads passes through its model provider, and the owner accepts this”
open_points.question: Which external model-provider boundary is accepted, what Registry data may cross it, and does the acceptance include provider retention, logging and subprocessors?
options: A specifically named provider under stated data-handling terms
Any provider selected by the owner, with all operator-visible data permitted
Only providers configured for no retention and no training
open_points.default_guess: Treat the provider as owner-selected, explicitly configured infrastructure and permit only the data required for the operator action.

open_points.subject: host administrative access
open_points.text: The owner “as the host's administrator” changes configuration, and the agent uses “the owner's own access to Registry's host”, but the listed secrets are only service tokens and the staff credential
open_points.question: What authenticates administrative access to the host, who may hold or delegate it, and is that credential covered by the stated vault and non-disclosure rules?
options: A separately managed host login credential held only by the owner
A delegated host credential with narrower permissions for the operator
The same staff credential also authenticates host access
open_points.default_guess: Use a separate host-administration credential held by the owner and managed outside Registry.

open_points.subject: deployment exposure check
open_points.text: “The owner's deployment definition enforces this” and “the owner checks it when deploying”, but “no component detects an exposure” and Registry starts normally either way
open_points.question: What concrete deployment check establishes that no Registry port is reachable beyond the host, what observable result constitutes success, and what happens when the check fails?
options: A documented manual reachability check that blocks deployment acceptance
An automated deployment test that must pass
No verification beyond inspecting deployment configuration
open_points.default_guess: Require a documented reachability check whose failure leaves the deployment unaccepted.

open_points.subject: configuration activation
open_points.text: “a change takes effect when the instance restarts”
open_points.question: What does Registry do at restart when credentials, frontend origin or artifact vocabulary configuration is absent, malformed, duplicated or internally inconsistent?
options: Fail startup without serving requests
Start with only valid entries and report rejected entries
Start in a restricted mode with writes disabled

open_points.subject: secret generation
open_points.question: What formats, minimum entropy and generation mechanism make a staff credential or service token acceptable to Registry?
options: Registry-defined opaque random-token requirements
Any non-empty owner-chosen string
Externally generated signed credentials with a defined scheme
open_points.default_guess: Accept opaque random tokens subject to a documented minimum entropy and format.
